one_liner: AVX-512 SIMD CSV parser for Go; drop-in encoding/csv replacement, faster only on unquoted data.
what_it_does: It's a Go CSV reader/writer meant to replace the standard library's encoding/csv for higher ReadAll throughput. The API is a same-name drop-in: swap the import for `csv github.com/nnnkkk7/go-simdcsv` and Reader/Writer, Comma, LazyQuotes, TrimLeadingSpace, etc. all work unchanged. It also exposes lower-level `ParseBytes`/`ParseBytesStreaming` for parsing a `[]byte` directly without going through `io.Reader`.
how_it_is_fast: It scans input in 64-byte AVX-512 chunks (`scanBuffer`), building bitmasks for quote/comma/CR/LF positions instead of branching byte-by-byte, then derives the in-quotes region with a prefix-XOR computed via PCLMULQDQ carryless multiplication (the simdjson-style structural-character technique) before locating field boundaries and materializing strings. `useAVX512` is checked once at init via a CPU feature test, with an automatic scalar fallback when AVX-512 (F/BW/VL) isn't available.
when_to_use: Go services that already deploy on amd64 hardware with AVX-512 (AMD Zen4+/EPYC 9x, Intel Skylake-X+)
Large, mostly-unquoted CSV (logs, numeric exports) at 10K-100K+ row scale, where the README shows +35% ReadAll throughput
You can pin CI/prod to Go 1.26+ built with the experimental GOEXPERIMENT=simd flag
You want the raw-bytes path (ParseBytes/ParseBytesStreaming) to skip io.Reader overhead entirely
You're prototyping or benchmarking SIMD CSV techniques in Go rather than shipping a production dependency
when_not_to_use: Production systems that can't accept a dependency the README itself calls experimental and 'not recommended for production use'
Any deployment target without AVX-512 F/BW/VL: Apple Silicon/ARM64, pre-Zen4 AMD, pre-Skylake-X Intel, and most hosted CI runners (ubuntu-latest included) — you get the scalar path with no speedup
Heavily-quoted CSV: the README's own numbers show ~30% slower than encoding/csv on all-quoted 10K-row data due to extra validation passes
Teams that can't carry an experimental Go toolchain flag (GOEXPERIMENT=simd) through their build pipeline
Anyone needing a stable API long-term: `simd/archsimd` is called out as unstable across Go releases, and the project is very young (47 stars, first tagged releases only recently)

integration.dependencies: none beyond stdlib and Go's experimental simd/archsimd package
integration.platforms: amd64 only for the SIMD path (requires AVX-512 F/BW/VL); falls back to a scalar implementation elsewhere, including arm64/Apple Silicon
integration.thread_safety: not documented — mirrors encoding/csv, whose Reader/Writer are not documented as safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: the Reader/Writer API is a same-name substitute for encoding/csv with all standard options supported, but unlike stdlib it requires Go 1.26+ and an experimental compiler flag (GOEXPERIMENT=simd), and the SIMD code path only activates on AVX-512 hardware

gotchas: SIMD source files are gated behind the `goexperiment.simd && amd64` build tag, so the fast path only compiles/activates under GOEXPERIMENT=simd on amd64; everywhere else you silently get the scalar implementation
All-quoted-field CSV is ~30% slower than encoding/csv (10K-row case) — the opposite of the headline speedup

Published AVX-512 numbers come only from a manually-triggered self-hosted CI workflow (ci-avx512.yml); the default per-PR CI (ubuntu-latest) runs scalar-only and doesn't exercise or verify the SIMD path
`simd/archsimd` is an experimental Go package the README warns 'may have breaking changes in future Go releases'
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It's the only Go-language entry in this category (siblings are .NET/Rust/Python/R/CLI tools) and the closest analog to the Rust `simd-csv` crate's idea applied to Go's encoding/csv. Pick it over cisv/zsv/xan/qsv only when you need an in-process Go library rather than a CLI tool, your data is mostly unquoted, and you can run on AVX-512 hardware with an experimental Go build.
verified_claims_summary: Verifier confirmed the README's ReadAll throughput table (e.g. 228->309 MB/s unquoted, 10K rows; +35%) against public paired Stdlib/SIMD benchmarks in benchmark_test.go, run with `go test -bench=. -benchmem` on Go 1.26 + GOEXPERIMENT=simd, AMD EPYC 9R14 (AVX-512), via a manually-triggered self-hosted CI workflow; the reported -30% regression applies specifically to the 10K-row all-quoted-fields case.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-06-14, MIT-licensed) but the author labels it experimental and 'not recommended for production use'; at 47 stars it's better treated as a technique to read or vendor selectively than a dependency to adopt outright.
